headline: Asset-sale gains supercharge profit as dividend rises
summary_short: Omega's Q2 2026 revenue rose 16.2% y/y to $328.2M and net income jumped 165.6% to $362.8M, mostly on a $246.5M gain from selling 26 facilities; core operating income grew a steadier 17.7% y/y. The board also raised the quarterly dividend to $0.68/share from $0.67.
summary_long: Rental income grew on 2025-26 acquisitions/escalations (+$16.4M), fewer straight-line write-offs (+$8.7M), and higher Maplewood cash rent (+$2.2M), lifting revenue 16.2% y/y; operating income rose a steadier 17.7% as G&A rose on $14.7M of stock comp and $4.2M of leadership-transition costs. Net income, EBIT, EBITDA and EPS roughly doubled or more, but that's overwhelmingly the $246.5M gain on selling 26 facilities (vs $22.9M a year ago), not core improvement. Interest expense fell on 2025 debt repayments. Cash fell to $39.0M (from $734.2M) as financing activities used $584.8M in H1 2026 vs providing $241.3M in H1 2025; equity rose 8.1% y/y to $5.39B. No FFO/AFFO guidance is given; the board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.68/share from $0.67.

drivers.explanation: Results reflect a sharp jump in gains on real estate dispositions ($246.5M vs $22.9M a year ago) layered on steady core rental growth from 2025-26 acquisitions and lease escalations.

Rental income rose on 2025-26 acquisitions/escalations (+$16.4M), fewer straight-line write-offs (+$8.7M), higher Maplewood cash rent (+$2.2M), and GBP strength (+$0.6M), partly offset by facility transitions (-$1.1M).
Not explained in the release as a standalone line; tracks the same revenue growth discussed above.
Revenue growth was partly offset by higher G&A ($14.7M incremental stock comp, $4.2M leadership-transition costs) and higher D&A from acquisitions and capital additions.
Driven overwhelmingly by the $246.5M gain on selling 26 facilities in the Triple-Net segment this quarter, versus a $22.9M gain in Q2 2025 — not a core-operations improvement.
The release attributes the jump in other income to a $223.6M increase in gain on assets sold, partly offset by lower interest income on short-term investments and FX/derivative losses.

H1 2026 financing activities used $584.8M of cash (vs providing $241.3M in H1 2025) while investing activities generated $282.0M (vs using $444.3M) on asset-sale proceeds — a swing consistent with the lower cash balance.
Not explained in the release as a standalone roll-forward; broadly consistent with retained net income and ATM/DRCSPP stock issuance exceeding dividends paid.
